role: Highways defect triage officer at a district council, reviewing one pothole report at a time
setting: A council highways team receives pothole reports from the public, councillors, its own inspectors and utility contractors. For each report the triage officer checks the logged location against the asset register, any site inspection, past works at the same spot, planned schemes and temporary measures, and any works order already raised. The officer then decides whether the defect meets intervention criteria, whether it is a failed earlier repair, what to do with the report now, and how quickly policy requires a response.

meets_threshold.instructions: Inspected defect depth meets the intervention depth for this road.

criteria.true: Recorded inspection depth at or above the listed threshold
criteria.false: Depth below threshold, or no valid inspection measurement

repeat_failure.instructions: This defect is a recurrence of an earlier completed repair here.

criteria.true: Completed prior repair confirmed within ten metres of defect
criteria.false: No prior repair matched, or match only approximate

next_step.instructions: What should the triage officer do with this report now?

criteria.close_no_action: Close the report: below criteria, duplicate, or already repaired.
criteria.request_inspection: Obtain a valid site measurement before deciding on any repair.
criteria.order_repair: Raise or confirm a works order, timed around planned schemes.
criteria.escalate_engineer: Refer to a highways engineer for claims, injury or recurring failure.

staff_effort.instructions: How much staff time would fully resolving this record require?
criteria: Under one hour of staff time needed
One to eight hours of staff time
One to five working days of staff time
More than five working days of staff time

response_timescale.instructions: Within what timescale does policy require the defect to be addressed?
criteria: No repair required under current intervention policy
Routine repair within 28 days of inspection
Priority repair within five working days
Make safe within 24 hours of report

factors.name: road_category
factors.description: Hierarchy class of the road from the asset register; sets the intervention depth and the response bands

factors.name: depth_vs_threshold
factors.description: How the inspected depth compares with the category intervention depth, including values within 2 mm of the boundary

factors.name: inspection_state
factors.description: Whether a valid site inspection exists: done after the report, only scheduled, never done, or dated before the report was received, so it measured an earlier condition

factors.name: prior_repair_match
factors.description: Past completed repair near the defect: none, the same spot within guarantee, the same spot after guarantee expired, or nearby with only an approximate location

factors.name: temporary_make_safe
factors.description: A temporary fill or barrier is already in place and in date; it lowers urgency without removing the need for a permanent repair

factors.name: planned_scheme_soon
factors.description: Resurfacing or patching that covers the defect location is programmed to start within 28 days

factors.name: duplicate_count
factors.description: Number of other open reports logged against the same location; alarming on its face but often just duplicates

factors.name: reporter_source
factors.description: Origin of the report; own-inspector reports carry measurements, public reports often lack them

factors.name: injury_or_claim
factors.description: An injury, vehicle damage or a compensation claim is linked to the location

factors.name: order_status
factors.description: State of any existing works order: none, raised, partially complete, or completed but awaiting sign-off

factors.name: defect_width_mm
factors.description: Surface width of the defect; a decoy that looks alarming but does not drive policy thresholds

factors.name: photo_attached
factors.description: Whether the report carries a photo reference; absent photos weaken public-only reports

sections.name: report
sections.description: Report id, received timestamp, source channel, photo reference, linked duplicate ids, claim flag

sections.name: location
sections.description: USRN, road category, intervention_depth_mm from the asset register, grid reference, speed limit

sections.name: inspection
sections.description: Inspector id, inspected_at date, depth_mm, width_mm, position offset; null when no inspection exists

sections.name: works_history
sections.description: List of past completed jobs at the street: job id, completed date, offset, guarantee_end

sections.name: programme
sections.description: Planned schemes with start dates and extents, plus temporary measures with installed and expiry dates

sections.name: current_order
sections.description: Existing works order id, raised date, status, completed_items and total_items; null if none

rendering_notes: road_category appears as location.road_class, and the threshold as location.intervention_depth_mm; the record never says whether the threshold is met, so the reader must compare it with inspection.depth_mm. depth_vs_threshold sets inspection.depth_mm relative to that threshold, with boundary cases differing by 0 to 2 mm. inspection_state: completed_valid gives a full inspection object dated after report.received_at; scheduled gives inspection with depth_mm null and a future inspected_at labelled scheduled_for; not_done gives inspection: null; dated_before_report gives a full object whose inspected_at precedes received_at. prior_repair_match puts a works_history entry whose offset_m is within 10 m (same spot) or given only as a street-level null offset (nearby_unconfirmed), and guarantee_end falls after or before the report date. temporary_make_safe adds a programme.temp_measures entry covering the offset with an expiry date in the future (or omits it); planned_scheme_soon adds a programme.schemes entry whose extent covers the offset and whose start date falls within 28 days, while decoy schemes on other extents or starting later appear in both cases. duplicate_count is the length of report.linked_reports, which is a decoy for urgency. reporter_source is report.channel; own_inspector reports usually come with inspection filled. injury_or_claim is report.claim_ref (string id or null). order_status fills current_order with status and completed_items/total_items (partial when completed_items < total_items), and there is no priority field. defect_width_mm is inspection.width_mm and is a decoy. photo_attached is report.photo_ref or null. No field ever states urgency, priority, repeat-failure status, recommended action or whether criteria are met; all must be inferred by comparing fields across sections.
